newsitem.title: GERMANY: Audi won't comment on reports CEO to leave.
newsitem.headline: Audi won't comment on reports CEO to leave.

text.p: Audi AG, a unit of Volkswagen, would not comment on Tuesday on reports that its management board chairman Herbert Demel was leaving to take up a senior post at the parent company.

"We never comment on speculation," an Audi spokesman said on Tuesday, but he did confirm that the Audi supervisory board would meet in the Hungarian town of Gyor on Wednesday and that personnel would be discussed at the meeting.

Several newspapers reported recently that Demel, an Austrian who had been in charge at Audi for two-and-a-half years, would give up his position at Audi and take up responsibility for Volkswagen's Latin American business.
On Wednesday last, Audi's marketing director Graham Morris said he wanted to leave the board for family reasons.

The spokesman said that there could be a decision at the supervisory board meeting on a possible new Audi factory in Brazil. Sources in the motor industry say that the plant would involve a triple-digit million-mark investment.

Audi has long planned a car production plant in the dollar region to better latch on to the U.S. market. In 1995 Audi sold nearly 3,400 vehicles in Latin America, with the main market in Brazil. VW sells around 700,000 vehicles in the dollar region, the Audi spokesman said.
